messages:
Sam Bennett: Heads up — during my evening watch we got a P1 page for elevated 5xxs from the routing layer affecting a small subset of customers (VIP routing group). I triaged briefly: the KV cache leader in eu-west-1 started returning intermittent 500s, which cascaded to our routing fallback and triggered higher latency then 5xxs. Noted in the incident: service:router-proxy, region:eu-west-1, impacted path:/v1/generate.

Marta (oncall-bot): :rotating_light: PagerDuty triggered (P1) — page id PD-5521 — 5xx spike eu-west-1 on router-proxy. Escalation policy: primary -> secondary -> SRE lead.

Sam Bennett: Quick timeline: 20:02 UTC — first anomaly in metrics; 20:07 UTC — PagerDuty page; 20:10 UTC — I pinned the problem to kv-cache leader process on node gpu-eu-05 (OOM-ish logs). I tried a graceful restart (`systemctl restart redwood-kv`) and watched logs: we saw immediate reduction in errors but the leader elected new primary and a small lag in replication caused a handful of failed reads for ~90s.

Priya Rao: Thanks Sam. For handoff: I'm taking primary for the next 2 hours. Current status?

Sam Bennett: Current status (20:26 UTC): routing errors down to baseline, no elevated 5xxs for the last 6m, but we still see elevated p95 on kv read latency (2x usual) for eu-west-1. KV nodes are healthy overall, leader change completed. I triggered a controlled node-swap and limited traffic to Dedicated pool for VIP routing via:
```
# move VIP routing to dedicated pool (temporary)
curl -X POST https://console.internal.redwood/api/v1/routing/routemove \
  -d '{"route":"vip-eu-west","target":"dedicated-pool-3","reason":"mitigation:kv-leader-flap"}' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP'
```
This dropped immediate customer errors. Customer-facing systems are currently on dedicated pool-3 (expected capacity ok).

Jordan: Who owns the KV runbook steps for leader flaps? I want to make sure we don't miss replication health checks.

Ethan Li: I own that runbook. Link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-leader-flap. TL;DR checks: replication_lag, mem_used, file_desc_count, and check system journal for repeated OOM kills. If you see replication_lag > 2000ms for > 2m, consider draining and reprovisioning node.

Priya Rao: OK — I'll continue as primary. Sam, please add any action items you started.

Sam Bennett: Action items done/in-progress: 
- Restarted redwood-kv on gpu-eu-05 and watched follower election. (done)
- Moved VIP routing to dedicated-pool-3 (done)
- Created a short-lived graph to capture read-error traces and associated request ids. (in progress)
- Opened a support ticket with infra to check for underlying host memory pressure/oom patterns: infra ticket #INF-1987 (in progress)

Marta (oncall-bot): Incident PD-5521 status updated: "Mitigated - rerouted VIP traffic to dedicated pool, monitoring."

Priya Rao: Current ask for handoff: 1) Monitor p95 for kv reads in eu-west-1 for next 30m. 2) If p95 > 2x baseline or 5xxs reappear, escalate to SRE lead and consider full node reprovision (runbook step 4). 3) Keep customer success updated if any regression.

Lee Park: Noted. I'm secondary for next 4h — will cover if Priya needs to step out. I'll also check the infra ticket once PRI loops infra.

Jordan: One more — check canary keyspace replication separately. We had a case last month where leader election didn't replicate meta keys and caused routing lookup misses. Run: `redis-cli -h gpu-eu-05 INFO replication` and verify `role:master` + `connected_slaves`.

Ethan Li: Good call. Also watch for excessive file descriptor counts: `lsof | wc -l` > 120k has bitten us before.

Sam Bennett: Customer impact summary (to include when we update CS): ~30 min of elevated 5xx for ~12 VIP customers routed through eu-west-1; all customer retries were served by fallback or by Dedicated pool after the reroute. No data loss. Actionable mitigation prevented larger outage.

Priya Rao: Handoff checklist for me -> Jordan/Lee: 
- Primary: Priya Rao (monitoring, communication)
- Secondary: Lee Park (escalation, infra liaison)
- SRE lead on call: Ethan Li
- Runbooks: KV leader flap (Ethan) and Routing fallback (https://redwood.internal/runbooks/routing-fallback)
- Current open tickets: INF-1987 (infra), PD-5521 (incident)
- Customer comms: prepare short note for affected VIPs if we see any recurrence — tag @cs-esc for draft.

Jordan: I'll add the canary keyspace check to the monitoring dashboard and create an alert if replication lag > 1s for 3 consecutive windows.

Priya Rao: Next steps for overnight: 
1) Keep traffic on dedicated-pool-3 for VIPs until infra confirms host stability (expected review in 2h). 
2) If infra determines host OK, we will gradually shift VIP routing back via `routemove` in 10% increments, monitoring errors. 
3) If any 5xxs return during shift, abort and move back to dedicated pool immediately. 

Sam Bennett: FYI: I captured request ids and logs -> saved to /var/tmp/pd-5521-traces.tar.gz and uploaded to internal incident bucket s3://redwood-incidents/pd-5521/traces.tar.gz. Link in ticket INF-1987.

Marta (oncall-bot): Reminder: Please use the incident postmortem template after incident is closed: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/template. Postmortems are due within 72 hours for P1s.

Priya Rao: OK handoff complete — I'm monitoring the dashboards now. Sam — thanks for the detailed notes. If anything changes I'll ping in this thread. :thumbsup:

Sam Bennett: Thanks — reaching out to infra and CS. Leaving handoff in this thread so logs + commands are all in one place. Good luck Priya.

Lee Park: Acknowledged. I'll watch the infra ticket and be ready to reprovision if INF says flapping persists.

Ethan Li: I'll stand by as SRE lead — if replication-lag alerts trigger, call me and I'll coordinate reprovision. Also adding a short playbook note to the runbook for 'move to dedicated pool' steps.

Priya Rao: Last note: coverage gap — EU night shift starts at 02:00 UTC and primary will be rotation-based. If we still have elevated p95 at that time, we'll extend handover with explicit 'continue monitoring' line in the shift log.

Sam Bennett: Closing my shift now. Thread left open for followups.
